findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. `time_records._summarised` preserves actor names but writes no login fields into the summary. When that summary contains `started_by` or `approved_by`, this line returns the absent login field without checking the actor's recorded commit or email. A past item with a known GitHub identity therefore shows a name and a null login after normal history compaction, contrary to the past-work requirement.
findings.title: Not done: known logins disappear when past work is compacted

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Scale. For each visible actor whose git email is not a GitHub noreply address, this line starts a separate `gh api` request. `machine_board` calls `person_login` for both starter and approver on every row, and the per-commit cache lasts only one minute. A board with 50 visible parts can therefore make roughly 100 serial GitHub requests on a normal read and repeat them after the cache expires.
findings.title: Serial commit lookups make board reads slow as the team grows

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. Both parameterized cases create and assert a new story and task after client setup. The earlier-adoption case upgrades the fixture, but never reads an item that predates the upgrade or has a compacted actor summary. The test therefore passes with the past-work login loss described above, leaving the named past-work proof absent.
